name: The Delta 72
label: Touch and Go
lede: Gregg Foreman moved to D.C. for Fugazi, bought a Farfisa, and built a band that played Booker T. soul like punk rock, with the White Stripes and the Strokes opening.

eras.title: An organ, some roommates and a Dischord single
eras.text: D.C. in 1994 was Fugazi's town, and Foreman had moved there for that. The band he started with his roommates wanted something else: punk, country, '60s R&B and an electric organ, all at once.

years.cap: The Delta 72: Foreman, Azzara, Stolfa and Thompson
years.src: Ink 19: The Delta 72 · Wikipedia: The Delta 72 · Wikipedia: Gregg Foreman
years.h: Gregg Foreman buys "this crazy organ" and starts a band
years.p: Ben Azzara drums, Sarah Stolfa plays Farfisa, and Kim Thompson of Cupid Car Club joins on bass. Cassettes sell on tour before there's a record.
years.xp:
"DC was really punk in the Fugazi way, which is cool, I moved there for that," Foreman told Ink 19 in 2000. The idea was a band "we ourselves would really want to see."

He grew up on his mom's soul records (she'd interned at Motown before he was born) and his dad's Stones and Flying Burrito Brothers. Purple Rain made him want a guitar; Black Flag's Damaged was the rebellion. He came up through Philadelphia's goth and post-punk scenes, and by the mid-'90s was also writing for Philadelphia City Paper.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Delta 72 · Ink 19: The Delta 72
years.h: Dischord and Kill Rock Stars share the first single
years.p: On the Rocks comes out as a joint release by the two labels, and the band tours the U.S. and plays up and down the Northeast. Foreman heard Booker T. in it from the start.

years.h: Mule's drummer comes in, and Touch and Go signs them
years.p: Azzara leaves for The Capitol City Dusters. Jason Kourkounis, formerly of [[Mule|84189509-850d-428b-a8f0-1626cb0eabb3]], takes the drums as the band signs to Touch and Go.

eras.title: Inner Ear, then Bob Weston
eras.text: Two albums in two years on Touch and Go, the first made with D.C.'s house engineers, the second with Bob Weston and a horn section. The bass chair changed hands in between.

years.src: Discogs: The R&B Of Membership · Wikipedia: The Delta 72
years.h: Recorded at Inner Ear, mixed by Brendan Canty
years.p: Don Zientara and [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]]' Eli Janney engineer the February 1996 sessions; [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] of Fugazi mixes with the band. Pat Graham shot the photos.
years.xp: Luther Gray adds saxophone, and Jason Farrell did the graphics. The single Rich Girls... backed with Cinderella came out on Touch and Go the same year, and the debut LP reworks On the Rocks.

yt: Full set, Coney Island High, NYC, August 1997
years.h: Bruce Reckahn takes over bass from Kim Thompson
years.p: Thompson leaves after the first album; Reckahn plays bass for the rest of the band's run.

years.src: Discogs: The Soul Of A New Machine
years.h: Bob Weston engineers, and plays trumpet too
years.p: Mark Boyce of [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]] guests on clavinet and Rhodes, and the album ends with We Hate the Blues, nearly 11 minutes long.
years.xp: John Upchurch plays tenor and alto sax and Mark Greenerer vibes. Discogs credits the liner notes to John Sinclair. Touch and Go catalog number TG182.
play: The Soul of a New Machine

eras.title: Philadelphia, gospel singers and the end
eras.text: By 2000 the band were Philadelphia transplants with a new organ player, and Foreman was steering them toward Sly Stone and the MC5. Meanwhile their drummer was making a different kind of record in San Diego.

years.cap: The Delta 72 at the Pilot Light, Knoxville
years.src: Wikipedia: The Delta 72 · Discogs: The Soul Of A New Machine
years.h: Mark Boyce moves from guest to organist
years.p: Sarah Stolfa leaves, and Boyce, who'd played keys on The Soul of a New Machine, joins full time.
Hot Snakes began when [[John Reis|626e7b64-3035-4f58-92a6-49790f600e30]] recorded songs with the Delta 72's drummer, then called in his old bandmate Rick Froberg to sing.

years.h: Sorega Doushita, an EP on Touch and Go
years.p: A stopgap between albums, followed in 2000 by the 7-inch The Doctor Is In.

years.cap: The Delta 72 at the Pilot Light, Knoxville, c. 2000
years.src: Artrocker · Clash: The Delta 72's Gregg Foreman
years.h: The White Stripes and the Strokes open for them
years.p: Artrocker remembers the shows as theater: James Brown moves, acrobatics, people swinging from the ceiling, and future garage-revival headliners on the undercard.
Foreman told Ink 19 the singers sound "more eerie than religious." The Japanese edition on P-Vine adds four bonus tracks.
years.xp:
"Gospel singers make anything sound spiritual. Even us," Foreman said. He was already half a record into the next batch of songs, which he described as funky rock like early Sly and the Family Stone and the MC5, with a little Al Green in there.

His mom came to every show she could, he said, and seeing his picture in Rolling Stone was a big thing for her.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Delta 72 · Wikipedia: Hot Snakes
yt: Full set at Rudyard's, Houston, April 2001
years.p: Three albums, an EP and a run of singles, everything after the first single on Touch and Go. Kourkounis keeps drumming in Hot Snakes until 2003.

eras.title: Cat Power's musical director
eras.text: Foreman spent the next 25 years as a sideman, bandleader and DJ for other people's records, most of all Chan Marshall's. He died in Los Angeles in 2026.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gregg Foreman · NME: Tributes paid
years.p: He signs on with Chan Marshall's Dirty Delta Blues Band in 2006 and later becomes her musical director.
years.xp: Along the way he played with [[Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|d1ab8ca8-fb9f-4e78-a422-3cd5406dc0b1]], Pink Mountaintops, the Meek and the Black Ryder, joined James Williamson's Re-Licked project in 2015, and toured Europe with Gossip in 2019. He made an EP with Alan Vega of Suicide, hosted a radio show called The Pharmacy, and DJ'd mod and soul nights from Paris to Tokyo.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gregg Foreman · NME: Tributes paid · Clash: The Delta 72's Gregg Foreman · People
years.h: Gregg Foreman dies in Los Angeles at 53
years.p: He was found at his home. People reported that the cause of death was unknown. Cat Power wrote, "Gregg, where do we begin."
years.xp: Wesley Eisold of Cold Cave wrote that Foreman "lived a life that others only claim to have lived." Garbage, Crocodiles and Matador Records posted tributes too.
